procedure: Listen to the teacher’s explanation of system dynamics and how the simulation will be implemented.
Open the simulation tool on a computer or tablet.
Manipulate different variables in the simulation and analyze how the system reacts.
Record the variable settings and the system responses in observation notes.
Use an S-curve to review the results, drawing one only if it represents the results observed.
Reflect on how changes impact the entire system and discuss how its parts are integrated and balanced.
aim: To understand how variability affects a system of interest by changing variables in an interactive simulation and observing the system’s response.

viva.question: What is a system?
viva.answer: A system is a whole formed by interacting parts.

viva.question: What is a variable in a simulation?
viva.answer: A value or condition that can be changed in the simulation.

viva.question: Why should you record the variable settings?
viva.answer: So the system’s observed responses can be compared with the settings used.

viva.question: What does an S-curve represent in this activity?
viva.answer: A way to review results when the observed response has an S-shaped pattern.

viva.question: Will changing a variable always produce the same response in every simulation?
viva.answer: No. The response depends on the particular simulation and the variable changed.

viva.question: Why consider the parts of a system together?
viva.answer: Because interacting parts can affect the system as a whole.

apparatus: Computer or tablet with internet access
Online simulation tool, such as an ecosystem simulator
diagram: Draw a graph of the recorded response against time, label the horizontal axis “Time” and the vertical axis with the measured response and its unit, and mark an S-shaped pattern only if the readings show one.
title: Observing Variability in an Interactive Simulation
precautions: Change one variable at a time when comparing its effect.
Record the settings and responses accurately, using the same measurement units throughout.
Do not assume that a change will cause the same response in every simulation or model.
Use the device carefully and keep it away from liquids.
Draw an S-curve only if it is supported by the observed results.
result: The system’s observed response varied with the settings in the recorded trials. The direction and size of the response depend on the particular simulation and variables used.
